title: Leslie Cross, in his own words
text: Here is veganism in Leslie Cross's own words, from the founding letters he wrote for The Vegan between 1949 and 1955. In 1949: the principle of the emancipation of animals from exploitation by man. In 1951: the object of the Society shall be to end the exploitation of animals by man, and the word veganism shall mean the doctrine that man should live without exploiting animals. And in 1955: this principle, this doctrine, is concerned with one matter only. A big matter, it is true, but a clearly defined one: the matter of the right relationship between man and the animals. Veganism is itself a principle, from which certain practices naturally flow. But it is in itself a principle, and not a set of practices.
